questions.title: Cyclosporine's immunosuppressant mechanism
questions.question: Which of the following most accurately describes the immunosuppressant action of cyclosporine?

options.B: Blockade of tissue responses to inflammatory mediators
options.D: Inhibition of calcineurin mediated gene transcription of interleukins
options.E: Interference with MHC II-peptide activation of T cells

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cyclosporine suppresses, rather than activates, immune cell function; activating NK cells would work against, not produce, an immunosuppressant effect.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cyclosporine does not act by blocking tissue responses to already-released inflammatory mediators; its action is upstream, preventing the T cell from producing those mediators (interleukins) in the first place.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Increased IgG catabolism is not cyclosporine's mechanism; that description does not match calcineurin inhibition or any recognised cyclosporine action.
explanations.D: Correct. Cyclosporine binds cyclophilin, and this complex inhibits calcineurin, a phosphatase required to activate the transcription factor NFAT. Without active NFAT, T lymphocytes cannot transcribe the interleukin-2 gene and other cytokine genes. This blocks T-cell activation and proliferation, the basis of its immunosuppressant effect.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Cyclosporine does not interfere with MHC class II-peptide presentation to T cells; its target is intracellular, downstream of antigen recognition, at the calcineurin-NFAT signalling step within the T cell.

questions.learning_objective: State that cyclosporine inhibits calcineurin-mediated gene transcription of interleukins in T lymphocytes.

questions.title: Drug blocking soluble receptors of TNF-alpha
questions.question: Which of the following drugs acts by blocking soluble receptors of TNF-α?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Anakinra is an IL-1 receptor antagonist, blocking interleukin-1 signalling, not a TNF-alpha soluble receptor construct.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sulfasalazine is a non-biologic prodrug DMARD cleaved by gut bacteria into 5-aminosalicylic acid and sulphapyridine; it has no TNF-receptor-blocking mechanism.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Gold salts are an older conventional DMARD with a mechanism unrelated to TNF-alpha receptor blockade.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Methotrexate is a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor with broad antiproliferative and anti-inflammatory effects, not a TNF-alpha soluble receptor blocker.
explanations.E: Correct. Etanercept is a fusion protein built from the extracellular domain of the TNF receptor joined to an antibody Fc region. It acts as a soluble decoy receptor that binds circulating TNF-alpha. This blocks TNF-alpha from reaching its true cell-surface receptors, dampening the inflammatory cascade.

questions.learning_objective: Identify etanercept as the soluble TNF-alpha receptor fusion protein among these DMARDs.

questions.title: Tofacitinib's mechanism of action
questions.question: Which statement is the mechanism of action of tofacitinib that used for treatment of rheumatoid arthritis?

explanations.A: Incorrect. TNF-alpha inhibition describes drugs such as etanercept, infliximab or adalimumab, which act extracellularly on TNF-alpha or its receptor, not tofacitinib's intracellular mechanism.
explanations.B: Correct. Tofacitinib is an oral small-molecule Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor. It blocks intracellular JAK enzymes, interrupting the JAK-STAT pathway that carries cytokine receptor signals to the nucleus. This intracellular, downstream action distinguishes it from the extracellular biologic DMARDs.
explanations.C: Incorrect. IL-6 receptor inhibition describes tocilizumab, not tofacitinib, which works one step further downstream, inside the cell, rather than blocking a specific cytokine receptor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. IL-1 inhibition describes anakinra, not tofacitinib; tofacitinib's target is intracellular JAK signalling common to multiple cytokine receptors, not one specific interleukin's receptor.
explanations.E: Incorrect. CD80/86 inhibition (blocking T-cell costimulation) describes abatacept's mechanism, not tofacitinib's intracellular JAK-STAT-blocking action.

questions.learning_objective: State that tofacitinib works as an oral JAK inhibitor, blocking intracellular JAK-STAT cytokine signalling.

questions.title: Drug used as bridging therapy in arthritis
questions.question: Which of the following drug is used in bridging therapy in patient with arthritis?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Leflunomide is itself a conventional DMARD with its own delayed onset of action; it is not the fast-acting agent used to bridge the gap while a DMARD takes effect.
explanations.B: Correct. Corticosteroids provide rapid symptomatic relief and inflammation control. A slower-onset DMARD, such as methotrexate, takes weeks to months to reach its full disease-modifying effect. The steroid is then tapered once the DMARD has taken hold, the defining bridging-therapy role.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sulfasalazine is a conventional DMARD, itself slow-onset, not the rapid bridging agent used alongside it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Celecoxib provides symptomatic NSAID-type relief but is not specifically the bridging agent used to cover a DMARD's delayed onset in the way corticosteroids are.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Anakinra is a biologic DMARD (IL-1 receptor antagonist), not the short-term bridging agent used while a conventional DMARD's effect is awaited.

questions.learning_objective: Identify corticosteroids as the bridging therapy used for rapid relief while a slower-onset DMARD takes effect.

questions.title: Reason to avoid celecoxib in a rheumatoid arthritis patient
questions.question: Which of the following patient characteristics is the most compelling reason for avoiding celecoxib in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A history of alcohol abuse is not the specific, compelling contraindication being tested for celecoxib; celecoxib's most concerning risk relates to cardiovascular events, not hepatic effects from alcohol history.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A history of gout is not a contraindication to celecoxib; NSAIDs including COX-2 selective agents can be used in gout management, so this history does not argue against celecoxib specifically.
explanations.C: Correct. Selective COX-2 inhibitors like celecoxib carry an increased cardiovascular (thrombotic) risk. This comes from sparing platelet thromboxane while still inhibiting vascular prostacyclin, tilting the balance toward clotting. A history of myocardial infarction makes this cardiovascular risk the most compelling reason to avoid celecoxib.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Osteoporosis history is not a specific contraindication to celecoxib; it is unrelated to celecoxib's known risk profile.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Peptic ulcer disease history would actually favour celecoxib over non-selective NSAIDs, since celecoxib's COX-1-sparing profile reduces gastric ulcer risk; this option describes a reason to prefer, not avoid, celecoxib.

questions.learning_objective: Identify a history of myocardial infarction as the compelling reason to avoid celecoxib, given selective COX-2 inhibitors' cardiovascular risk.

questions.title: Drug inhibiting phagocytic function and stabilising lysosomes
questions.question: Which of the following inhibit phagocytic function and stabilize lysosomes:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Abatacept blocks T-cell costimulation by binding CD80/86, an entirely different mechanism from lysosomal stabilisation or phagocyte inhibition.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Anakinra is an IL-1 receptor antagonist, working extracellularly on cytokine receptor binding, not through lysosomal membrane effects.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Leflunomide inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, blocking pyrimidine synthesis, a metabolic mechanism unrelated to lysosomal stabilisation or phagocyte function.
explanations.D: Correct. Chloroquine raises lysosomal pH and stabilises lysosomal membranes. This inhibits phagocytic cell function and interferes with antigen processing and presentation. That interference is the mechanism behind its antirheumatic action.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, a folate-antagonist mechanism affecting cell proliferation, not a lysosome-stabilising or phagocyte-inhibiting one.

questions.learning_objective: Identify chloroquine as the DMARD that inhibits phagocytic function and stabilises lysosomal membranes.

questions.title: DMARD responsible for retinopathy
questions.question: Which of the following DMARDs is responsible for retinopathy?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Sulfasalazine's characteristic risks are gastrointestinal and haematological (such as agranulocytosis), not retinopathy.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Leflunomide's characteristic risks are hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity, not an ocular retinal toxicity.
explanations.C: Correct. Hydroxychloroquine accumulates in the retinal pigment epithelium over years of use. This accumulation can cause irreversible retinopathy if unrecognised. That risk is why long-term users require baseline and periodic ophthalmologic screening.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cyclosporine's characteristic risk is nephrotoxicity (along with hypertension and tremor), not retinopathy.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Etanercept's characteristic risks relate to immunosuppression, chiefly infection and malignancy risk, not a retinal toxicity.

questions.learning_objective: Identify hydroxychloroquine as the DMARD whose defining adverse effect is retinopathy, requiring ophthalmologic screening.
